Fake World Assets (FWA) is an incredibly interesting mechanic + worth observing

but my concern is what happens when the FWA price reverses…

Right now the reflexivity works in its favour:

Activity → FWA rewards → higher $ value of those rewards → better LP returns → more attractive NFTs deposited → better gacha experience → more activity

The problem is that same flywheel can spin backwards (see diagram):

FWA price ↓ → depositor rewards worth less → LP returns compress → fewer attractive NFTs enter the pool → pool quality deteriorates → gacha EV / excitement falls → fewer spins → lower fees → lower ETH yield for depositors → lower protocol revenue → less potential buyback demand → FWA price ↓

The 15-day bootstrap makes this particularly interesting, with 30% of supply distributed between depositors and purchasers before the model transitions towards protocol-revenue-funded buybacks

The real test for FWA therefore isn’t whether the incentive design can bootstrap activity, it’s whether that activity remains once the value of the subsidy falls

Is the protocol attractive without FWA incentives?

If yes, FWA is an accelerator for an underlying economic engine

If no, FWA is subsidising activity and the reflexivity that made the launch so powerful can work just as aggressively in reverse

Death spiral backstop solution: 

Direct a portion of protocol revenue to LPs in ETH rather than routing it all through FWA buybacks, creating a token-price-independent yield floor that keeps quality NFTs deposited even if FWA falls

Yeah, @Rain__Protocol is one of the most intriguing infra protocols rn... But dayum, tokenomics is a huge risk here.

42.45% of RAIN remains locked, yet to enter the market.

Evidence from @Tokenomist_ai:

• Total supply: 1.15 trillion RAIN; circulating: ~662 billion (57.6% unlocked); locked: ~488 billion (42.5%)

• Market cap: $9.35B; FDV: $16.3B.

• Near-term releases: ~40.4B RAIN unlocking in Aug 2026 (3.5% of supply) and ~90.1B over the next three months (Aug–Oct 2026).

• Protocol mechanics: 2.5% burn on traded volume; current daily volume ≈ $28.9M (~2.05B RAIN/day), implying ~51M RAIN burned/day (~1.53B/month).

Let me explain why I'm watching this.

Unlocks add new supply to markets; cliffs create short, concentrated pressure while linear vesting creates steady supply flow.

RAIN has experienced both: a large cliff in Sep 2025 and now smaller, regular monthly releases (tens of billions of RAIN).

Put another way: burn offsets roughly 3.8% of current monthly unlock velocity.

To reach parity the protocol would need a massive increase in trading volume – on the order of tens of times current activity – or a materially higher burn rate.

Absent that, net supply rises each month.

@Rain__Protocol is a great infra thing – but the inflation risk is structural, not binary.

RAIN carries a meaningful, predictable dilution profile today.

That’s not fatal if adoption accelerates, but the current burn mechanism is far too small to neutralize scheduled unlocks without major growth.

These are not people that are flying fast and loose, they are methodically investing in their edge.

They are going to get massively rewarded.

Google has an incredible search experience. They seem to be navigating this transition to use AI. They have an incredible cloud business, and they have an incredible silicon business.

The best thing that can happen to them is 500 different models proliferate, and they support all of them. Because they will make so much money at the silicon layer, they'll make so much money as the cloud provider, and they'll find a bunch of apps, including YouTube and other things, to make money from because you use the AI to target ads better or to help make better content, etc., etc.

Jason:

“Fragmentation is good for them.”
